text:
sam: Quick share — ran a regional bench for the new model bring-up (dragon-7b quantized) comparing the live/streaming path vs poll/one-shot HTTP across A100 and H100 in us-west1 + eu-west1. Charts/output: https://go/reports/20653. TL;DR: streaming wins on p50 but loses a lot of throughput/GPU and can blow up p99 for long contexts due to KV-cache growth and smaller effective batch sizes.

maya: Can you paste the headline numbers? want to see absolute deltas.

sam: Paste of key points (short):
- us-west1 A100 fp16 poll/non-stream: peak 360 rps/GPU, p50 48ms, p95 120ms, p99 230ms
- us-west1 A100 fp16 streaming/live: peak 140 rps/GPU, p50 28ms, p95 190ms, p99 420ms
- eu-west1 H100 int8 poll/non-stream: peak 420 rps/GPU, p50 42ms, p95 100ms, p99 210ms
- eu-west1 H100 int8 streaming/live: peak 165 rps/GPU, p50 25ms, p95 160ms, p99 380ms
(bench runs used steady 8k concurrency fanouts, 2k short/6k long prompts mix)

rajesh: Interesting — int8 recovers throughput, but streaming p99 still worse. Which kernel/config set did you use for each path?

sam: Non-stream path used batched execution with Triton fused matmul kernels + cublas fallback (batcher groups up to 512 tokens). Streaming path uses continuous batching + KV cache pinned per-connection; we softpin to cuda-streams v2 to avoid STALLs. On H100 we forced kernel_profile = "tensorcore_fast" which reduced p50 by ~8-10ms.

emily: Any quality regressions from int8 quant? we need to log against eval suite.

sam: Small regressions: median EM drop ~0.6% vs fp16, most issues on arithmetic / precise-token tasks. Eval suite id eval/arith-2 flagged regressions on ~3% of testcases. Suggested mitigation: mixed-precision fallback for math tokens (quant.profile = int8-mixed -> fallback to fp16 on specified ops).

gabo: For capacity sizing (customer SLO p95 < 200ms) what do you recommend?

sam: Recommendations:
- If customer wants max throughput and p95 <200ms: use H100 int8 non-stream. 1 GPU ≈ 400 rps observed -> plan with 25% headroom => provision 1 GPU per ~300 rps.
- If customer requires streaming (low p50 priority): use H100 streaming path. 1 GPU ≈ 160 rps observed -> provision 1 GPU per ~120 rps for 25% headroom.
- Note: network variance matters — eu-west1 p99 ~10-15% worse than us-west1 in our runs due to cross-region tail and egress saturation at high fanout.

maya: Any recommended runtime config snapshots to store with the rollout?

sam: Configs to snapshot: autoscale.min=2, autoscale.max=20, batch.max_tokens=4096, stream.max_conns=1024, kernel_profile=tensorcore_fast (H100 only), quant.profile=int8-mixed (with fp16 fallback for math ops). Also capture batcher.window_ms=12 for non-stream and stream.batcher.max_delay_ms=6 for streaming to tune tail. I'll drop the full JSON runbook to /runbooks/bench-20653.json and link it in the report.

infra-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/bench/20653 -> infra-bench-ux; ETA ~12m.

rajesh: Thanks. One open item — can someone run the same bench with 4k+ context lengths (longer contexts) because I expect streaming p99 to worsen with KV growth; non-stream can still win with larger batch token amortization. @maya can you pick this up?

maya: Yep, starting the 4k run now (kickoff config: sample_rate=100, context=4096, mix=30% long). I'll post updated numbers in this thread once done. :rocket:
